Alphabet 2026 PM Summary
In 2025, Alphabet stock (up 65% y/y) outperformed major indices (S&P 500 up 16% and NASDAQ up 20%) and peers (Meta up 13%, Amazon up 5%, and Microsoft up 15%). Alphabet’s 2025 stock returns benefitted from a valuation re-rating and positive estimate revisions. Re-rating was driven by improved AI sentiment and a reduction of the search regulatory overhang (See our note: Remedy bite falls short of initial ruling bark; Less overhang = higher multiple). AI sentiment benefited from a successful launch of Gemini 3.0 LLM, improving AI related search traffic and search revenue upside, customer announcements indicating growing traction for TPUs, and Cloud wins that drove Cloud backlog upside.
In 2025, the S&P 500 broader market multiple increased by 2%, while Alphabet’s valuation multiple expanded by 38%. Additionally, Alphabet’s two-year forward EPS expectations increased by 24% 9to $11.21 from $9.00 from the start of 2025 driven by stronger topline growth and continued cost discipline.

Key debate: Appropriate valuation multiple for Alphabet give AI position
At $332, Alphabet is trading at ~27x our 2027 GAAP EPS (but just 21x for core business in our sum of parts analysis) vs S&P 500 at 21x (assuming $340 in 2027 EPS). Over the last 10 years Google has traded at a 4pts premium to the S&P 500 on GAAP EPS. With the stock valuation modestly above recent history, a key debate on Alphabet is if there is multiple expansion potential from here given the company’s strong AI position and longterm optionality from initiatives such as quantum computing, TPU sales, autonomous driving, etc., or valuation multiple risk given strong AI competition and an ongoing capex investment cycle.
For Bulls, AI as a new paradigm for economic growth and the top investment theme for the next 5 years. Alphabet is well positioned to drive outsized growth given positioning across foundational models, custom silicon, consumer distribution, and enterprise distribution. As both consumer and enterprise adoption of AI services increases, especially for Cloud, it could support more durable revenue growth (less cyclical) and a higher valuation. On the consumer side, AI will both increase consumer search activity, and also drive higher revenues through monetization of zero click searches and Agentic

For Bears, high-profile product launches by competitors across frontier models, AI-native search, hardware, and related areas, could quickly shift AI sentiment and prompt the Street to reassess Google’s relative AI positioning. For example, Nvidia’s Blackwell could enable the next generation of leading edge LLMs from competitors. Meanwhile, increasing usage of competitive AI products are structurally weakening Google’s moats in web indexing and distribution, increasing the risk of gradual query share erosion. Also, OpenAI’s ad launch in 2026 will drive a shift of search budgets, impacting Google’s longterm growth outlook. Finally, front-loaded infrastructure investments will pressure margins vs expectations, the EPS growth trajectory, and drive an unstainable FCF valuation, and risk of an industry capacity overbuild warrants a lower stock multiple. #2) Higher traffic monetization from AI-native formats
Per Datos (3Q’25 report), 98.9% of the Google desktop searches in the US and 98.6% of searches in UK & Europe do not result in a paid ad click. AI integration has significantly enhanced search functionality, evolving Search into a more intelligent, multi-modal assistant capable of handling complex tasks. This shift is allowing users to ask more nuanced and multi-step questions, driving higher search volumes, improving engagement, and enabling Google Search to better interpret underlying commercial intent. With a growing percentage of searches served in AI-native formats (AI Overviews, AI Mode, Gemini), and better AI models for delivering results, we see potential for better monetization of zero click queries to drive better search performance. In other words, we see potential for monetization of AI queries to go from Neutral vs traditional search, to better than traditional search.
How ads in AI Overviews and AI mode work?
Ads in AI native search formats are matched based on Google’s understanding of user intent, which is informed by both the user history, user query and the content of the AI-generated response. To help advertisers capture these opportunities, Google offers broad match or keywordless targeting, allowing ads to appear across a wider range of emerging AI searches.
For example, a query such as “why is my pool green and how do I clean it” may not be explicitly commercial or have relevant targeting keywords, and prior search results may have just shown links to articles with answers, and then a links to advertiser sites. However, AI Overviews, in addition to answering the question, may suggest more relevant actions within Google like testing water or vacuuming the pool. This creates new opportunities for advertisers to engage users on Google.

Smart Bidding Exploration extends ad reach beyond keywords
Google has introduced Smart Bidding Exploration, a major update to its bidding framework that expands advertisers’ reach by identifying and bidding on a broader range of high-intent search queries beyond traditional keyword targeting. Built on existing AI-powered tools like AI Max, Smart Bidding Exploration helps advertisers capture highperforming searches from new, unique categories. For example, a mortgage lender that previously bid on exact terms like “mortgage” or “home loan” can now use Smart Bidding Exploration to capture broader, but still relevant, queries such as “how to buy a home,” “best time to apply for a mortgage,” or “what credit score do I need to buy a house.” These are intent-rich, upper- to mid-funnel queries where AI should help Google to capture intent earlier in the decision-making process.

#3) Cloud upside with Gemini and TPU differentiation
Google’s vertically integrated AI stack that includes proprietary Gemini models and custom silicon can drive superior performance and cost efficiency for diverse AI use cases. This differentiation could drive higher enterprise win rates, translating into Cloud growth and profitability upside. We estimate Google Cloud revenues will grow 37% y/y in 2026 (vs Street 34% and 32% in 2025), and see opportunities for margin expansion with strong sector demand supporting high Cloud asset utilization.
Accelerating AI demand showing in rapidly growing Cloud backlog
In 3Q’25, Google Cloud backlog growth accelerated to 82% y/y (vs 37% y/y in 2Q) to $158bn. Growth should remain strong as, in October, Anthropic entered into a multi-year partnership with Google Cloud valued in the tens of billions of dollars, granting Anthropic access to up to 1mn TPUs. We note that Google Cloud backlog growth compares favorably to the company’s largest peers.

Gemini: Gemini 3.0 LLM is ranking among the leading frontier models and is increasingly emerging as a preferred choice for developers. As enterprises prioritize model quality, reliability, and integration with existing data and workflows, Gemini is becoming a core platform for building AI applications. As Gemini is accessible only through Google Cloud, the frontier model serves as an anchor product that drives incremental cloud consumption. #4) Well positioned for Agentic AI
Agents represent the next phase of AI evolution, and we think leadership in agentic AI will be critical for AI sentiment in 2026. We believe Google possesses all the core capabilities required to monetize AI-driven transactions at scale and is well positioned to lead in an agentic AI environment. Google’s integrated advertising stack, deep advertiser demand, and extensive merchant and partner relationships create a comprehensive structural advantage. These elements should enable Google to convert agent-driven actions into monetizable events by embedding sponsored recommendations and conversion-optimized outcomes directly at the point of user intent. As a result, we think Google is relatively better positioned than competing Big Tech platforms to drive higher monetization efficiency as agentic consumer ecosystems scale.
Agentic AI could structurally lift Search monetization
Currently, Google Search monetization is primarily click-based, with revenue tied to CPC and user traffic to third-party sites. However, growing user adoption of agentic AI solutions could change this model by executing tasks end-to-end, such as booking travel, purchasing products, or completing form-based workflows. This shift would enable Google to monetize at the point of transaction rather than at the point of intent, supporting higher-value CPA or revenue-share models that are more closely aligned with realized outcomes. While Google’s take rates are likely to be competitive (lower) to start, over time, this evolution could increase monetization per user by structurally improving conversion efficiency and allowing Google to capture a greater share of economic value per interaction.
